correctness.rationale: The domination criterion is exact: any set meeting at least two parts dominates, while a one-part set dominates only when it is the whole part. The security proof then exhausts support sizes. For two-part support, an attack in \(A_i\) fails exactly when the opposite support has one selected vertex and \(A_i\) has at least two omissions; the symmetric condition is necessary and sufficient. Inclusion-exclusion over these two bad events yields the pair polynomial. Direct exhaustive verification agrees on all 64,916 subsets of 128 complete-multipartite isomorphism types through order \(10\).

value.rationale: The complete multipartite secure domination number is known, but the full feasible-set distribution is a different natural invariant. The support theorem isolates the only two-part obstruction and yields every coefficient of a named secure domination polynomial in closed form. This is a structural classification over an arbitrary part-size vector, not a numerical table, arbitrary slice, or mere restatement of the known minimum.
